subject: dsa
title: Longest Common Subsequence
summary: dp[i][j] is the LCS length of the first i chars of text1 and the first j chars of text2. When the current chars match, extend the diagonal by one; otherwise carry the larger of the value above or to the left.
problem: Find the length of the longest common subsequence of text1 = "abc" and text2 = "ac". Rows are prefixes of text1 ("", a, b, c); columns are prefixes of text2 ("", a, c). dp[i][j] is the LCS of those prefixes.

steps.caption: Rows are text1 "abc", columns are text2 "ac". Row 0 and column 0 are the empty-prefix base, all 0.
Row 1 is char a. a vs a matches, so diagonal+1 = 1. a vs c differs, so carry max(top, left) = 1.
Row 2 is char b. b matches neither a nor c, so each cell carries max(top, left): both become 1.
Row 3 is char c. c vs a differs, carry 1. c vs c matches, so diagonal 1 + 1 = 2.
The bottom-right cell is 2, so the LCS length is 2 (the subsequence "ac").
